content.text:
So it's a static HTML app expected. Build a Metroidvania game in index.html (probably with separate js/css files, but static server supports js/css). The prompt is just a theme. We should build a polished, playable Metroidvania prototype set in NYC sewers. Need mobile support per Agents.md (Android/iOS responsive + touch controls).

Let me plan the game:

Title: "SUBSURFACE: Below the City" or "Sewer Knight: Five Boroughs". Metroidvania core: interconnected rooms, ability gates, map, save at checkpoints maybe, bosses.

Scope matters. A canvas 2D platformer with:
- Movement: run, jump, crouch? wall jump, dash, double jump, grapple? Abilities unlocked: Dash (Wall dash?), Double Jump, maybe "Steam Vent" glide.
- Interconnected room graph (tile-based rooms) with doors/gates colored by ability.
- Combat: melee pipe wrench swing, enemies (rats, sludge, cockroach knight, etc.), health, checkpoints.
- Boss: "The Croc King" in the deep sump, plus mini-boss maybe.
- Map overlay (M), pause, inventory ability list.
- Mobile touch controls: d-pad and action buttons, responsive canvas scaling.

Need to make it robust and visually attractive. Use pure canvas 2D with procedural pixel/vector art, no external assets. Add atmospheric lighting, parallax, dripping water, steam, neon green sludge. Audio via WebAudio procedural SFX/music (optional, toggle). Since autoplay restrictions, start on user gesture.

We should verify with playwright screenshot. Need to serve on port 3000 using start.sh? start.sh uses RUNTIME_DIR default. We can run `PORT=3000 node $RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs` in tmux per AGENTS. Check playwright availability and Xvfb. Use `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3000`. We'll capture screenshots and inspect.

The game needs a solid scope. Let's design details:

World: 2D tile grid, rooms 40x23 tiles? A metroidvania map of ~8-10 rooms, interconnected with doors. Camera per room? Use single continuous world per room with camera scroll, but simpler: rooms with camera following player clamped to room bounds. Persistent room state.

Could do a single large world with regions and camera; but map easier with room grid. Let's define rooms as tile maps generated from string rows. Each room 60x34 tiles at 16px = 960x544, nearly 16:9 960x540. Screen 960x540 logical. Camera fits whole room; players traverse. Interconnected via edge doors. That makes level design manageable and looks like classic Metroidvania rooms.

Actually camera-per-room with tile size 24 gives 60*24=1440 > 960, allowing scroll. Let's choose rooms 48x30 tiles, tile 24 => 1152x720, camera scrolls within room. Canvas 1152x648? Keep logical resolution 1280x720 and scale. Hmm mobile.

Design fixed internal resolution 960x540, tile=32? That gives 30x17 tiles per screen. Rooms 56x30 tiles = 1792x960, scroll. Tile 32 is nice for collision and art. Player 22x34.

World map graph:
- Room A: "Floodgate Junction" (start, save point) — central hub.
- Room B: "Rat Warrens" (east) — low level, rats; gate to "Tunnel 7".
- Room C: "Tunnel 7" (east) — dark, requires dash? Maybe use lantern? Keep abilities: Wall Jump, Dash, Double Jump.
- Room D: "Sump Pump" (below hub) — mini-boss "Sump Warden" grants double jump.
- Room E: "Steamworks" (west) — requires double jump to cross vents, grants dash.
- Room F: "The Overflow" (vertical shaft) — requires wall jump.
- Room G: "Croc's Lair" — boss, requires dash+double jump.
- Room H: "Maintenance Closet" — hidden room with health upgrade.

Progression path:
Start hub, go east into Rat Warrens, get wrench? Player starts with wrench. Find wall jump ability (Ivy? "Grip Gloves") in Tunnel 7 via rat warrens. Then Sump Pump mini-boss grants "Steam Boots" (double jump). Then Steamworks grants dash. Then boss lair.

Maybe 7 rooms. Keep levels moderate.

Rooms with gate colors:
- Wall jump gate (orange) in hub east high path.
- Double jump gate (cyan) vertical.
- Dash gate (magenta) long gap.

Map screen showing visited rooms as rectangles with connections, player marker.

Combat:
- Wrench melee, hitbox in front, 0.25s cooldown, knockback.
- Enemies: Rat (patrol, contact damage), Sludge Blob (hop), Turret "Steam Sentry" shooting projectiles, boss with phases.
- Player health 5 hearts, invuln frames, knockback, respawn at last save bench on death with enemies reset but abilities kept. Save benches restore health and save. Progress auto? Store in localStorage, plus continue.

Add collectibles "Golden Trash" (lore/money?) perhaps not needed. Health upgrade pickups: 2 "Bio-Cells".

Visual style: dark teal, warm sodium lights, green sludge, brick arches, pipes, dripping water, steam particles, puddle reflections, background NYC graffiti "NYC", "NO WAKE", scaffolding. Pixel-art vibe via canvas drawing shapes; maybe use low-res filter? Draw at internal res 960x540 then scale up with imageSmoothing disabled for crisp look. Use chunky rects and glow via gradients.

Rendering: layered:
- Background gradient / distant tunnel archways with parallax, pipes.
- Tiles: brick walls, floors, sloped? Keep rectangular tiles but draw pseudo arches.
- Water/sludge surface animated sine.
- Foreground vignette, film grain, drips.
- Lighting: player has warm lantern glow; neon signs.

Parallax based on room camera. Use precomputed decorations per room seeded random.

Controls:
- Keyboard: A/D or arrows move, Space/Z jump, J/X attack, Shift/K dash, W/up interact, M map, Esc pause. Maybe wall jump by jumping while touching wall.
- Mobile: on-screen left/right, jump, attack, dash; swipe? Use dedicated buttons. Map/pause icons. Hide when no touch? detect coarse pointer and show touch controls; also allow toggle.

Audio: WebAudio synth for jump, attack, hit, pickup, boss roar; ambient sewer drone loop generated; music maybe simple minor arpeggio. Provide mute button.

Need robust collision: AABB against tile grid with swept per-axis movement. Player physics with coyote time, jump buffering, variable jump height. Wall slide/jump when ability unlocked. Dash with cooldown and i-frames maybe.

Level data: Use tile maps as string arrays with characters:
'#' solid brick, '=' platform? 'X' gate tiles tied to ability? doors as objects. Place items, enemies, checkpoints, triggers via symbol map.

Rather than hand-author huge ASCII maps, generate procedurally with seeded room templates? Handcrafted feel is better. Each room 56 cols x 30 rows? That's a lot of typing but manageable with helper generation: define room with base floor/ceiling and add platforms via objects. Could define rooms via simple geometry arrays: solids rectangles, platforms, hazards, doors. This is easier and still looks good.

Let's create a level definition with:
room = { id, name, w=56, h=30 (tiles), theme, solids: [ [x,y,w,h] ], platforms?: spikes?, water?, background, doors: [{x,y,w,h,to, spawn}], entities, pickups }
Collision grid derived from rectangles. Visual tile rendering derived from grid: brick tiles near edges; draw big brick patterns.

Simplify: rooms of fixed height 30 (960 px at 32). Width varies 44-72 tiles. Camera clamped.

Map connectivity via doors at left/right edges or bottom/top.

Hub design (56x30):
- ground at y=26..30 (floor), ceiling y=0..3.
- central area, doors east at y=22 (2 tiles high? player 34px => 2 tiles 64 px high door), west etc.
- Save bench at x=8 ground.
- Wall-jump gate: high east ledge? Let's sketch.

Maybe use a data-driven room builder with helper functions: floor, ceiling, pillar, platform.

Rather than manually reason every tile coordinate in text, write JS with builder calls. E.g.:

const rooms = {
 hub: {
   name: 'Floodgate Junction', w: 56, h: 30, theme:'brick',
   build: (r) => {
     r.border(); // walls
     r.floor(26);
     r.solid(0,0,56,3);
     ...
   }
 }
}

We can implement border that leaves door openings; doors created after.

Doors: represented as rectangles where player overlaps and presses up? Classic: walk into door zone and it transitions. To prevent accidental transitions, use trigger at edge with small zone; auto-transition with fade. Use edge exits: when player reaches x<0 or x>world width, transfer. Door visuals as arched tunnel on walls. That's simplest: at sides, openings in walls; player walking into them triggers room change. Vertical via ladders? Could avoid vertical transitions except boss pit? Use only side exits, with some one-way? Metroidvania interconnection can be entirely horizontal edges. Rooms arranged in a grid: hub central, east warrens, further east tunnel7, west steamworks, west further? And below sump via door in hub floor? Could implement floor doors (falling through) easily: stepping onto a hole transition zone at bottom. Vertical shaft room maybe connected via bottom.

Let's define world map grid:
- (2,1) Hub "Floodgate Junction"
- (3,1) Rat Warrens (east of hub)
- (4,1) Tunnel 7 (east of warrens) — wall-jump ability at end; return path.
- (1,1) Steamworks (west of hub) — needs double jump? Actually gate...
- (2,2) Sump Pump (below hub) — mini-boss grants double jump.
- (2,0) The Overflow (above hub) — vertical, wall jump required, leads to boss? 
- (1,0) Croc's Lair? Hmm.

Simplify to 8 rooms:
Hub at (1,1)
Rats east (2,1)
Tunnel 7 (3,1) — wall-jump gloves
Steamworks west (0,1) — wall-jump gate (vertical section) -> dash boots
Sump below (1,2) — double jump (mini-boss), reached via hole in hub floor gated behind? Drop down; exit back up via ladder/vent.
Overflow above (1,0) — wall-jump climb, connects to boss lair.
Croc Lair (2,0) — boss, requires dash to cross gap.
Secret Closet (0,0) — health upgrade, requires dash from Croc area? Optional.
Maybe extra "Maintenance" small room (0,2) optional health.

Progression:
1. Start hub; go east through Rats to Tunnel 7 end -> "Grip Gauntlets" (wall jump).
2. Return hub; access high east wall door? Hmm wall jump gate: horizontal progression needs wall jump to climb a shaft in hub to upper door. Yet wall jump is found east — that's fine: backtrack to hub, climb shaft to Overflow.
Actually double jump found below; need access? Drop into sump early via hole; mini-boss tough but beatable with wrench; grants "Steam Boots" (double jump). Then wall jump in hub to upper area. Hmm order:
- Tunnel 7 (east) -> wall jump.
- Use wall jump in hub to reach upper door to Overflow.
- Overflow leads to Croc Lair, but boss door sealed requiring "3 valves"? Eh.

Better ability-gated path:
- Start hub. East door open -> Rat Warrens -> Tunnel 7; get wall jump at end.
- In Tunnel 7 deep area, wall jump lets you climb out and return with ability.
- Back in hub, wall jump up shaft to Overflow (vertical room).
- Overflow has a double-jump gate too high; drop down to Sump (below Overflow), fight Sump Warden -> double jump boots.
- With double jump, climb Overflow and cross to Steamworks? Hmm.

Alternatively get double jump in Tunnel 7 and wall jump in Steamworks.

Let's not overcomplicate; ability gates can be:
- Wall jump ability "Rust Grip" found in Tunnel 7.
- Double jump "Sump Boots" from miniboss in Sump Pump below hub (drop hole accessible from start; miniboss optional early).
- Dash "Pressure Valve" found in Steamworks, reachable only with wall jump (vertical shaft).
- Boss in Croc's Lair, reachable via Overflow with double jump + dash gate inside.

Map:
Hub (1,1) — doors: E rats, W steamworks (blocked by grate requiring wall jump? no, just open), bottom hole to Sump, upper-right door to Overflow requiring wall jump climb.
Rats (2,1) — enemies, E to Tunnel7, W to hub.
Tunnel7 (3,1) — wall jump pickup at far end; E dead end (locked grate "Borough line").
Steamworks (0,1) — vertical; wall jump needed to climb; dash pickup; W dead end.
Sump (1,2) — miniboss; double jump; exit up via vent back to hub.
Overflow (1,0) — tall climb with walljump + doublejump; leads E to CrocLair and W to secret.
CrocLair (2,0) — boss; requires dash to enter? Put sludge gap requiring dash.
Secret (0,0) — health upgrade.

Additional optional room Maintenance (0,2) health? Maybe enough content.

Maybe add one more room "The Grid" behind locked gate requiring 2 keys? Skip.

Boss fight: "GREASE CROC" / "THE CROCODILE KING" in flooded chamber; attacks: lunge, tail sweep, toxic spit, summon rats. 3 phases. Reward: clear ending screen "The city sleeps. For now." plus map completion.

Mini-boss "Sump Warden": big sludge with charge attack; gives Steam Boots.

Health upgrade pickups: +1 max health each (two in secret rooms).

Lore pickups: "Transit Tokens" optional collectible, or notes. Add notes for flavor.

Save: benches in hub and maybe one in Overflow; localStorage saves state: abilities, maxHp, visited rooms, collected items, boss defeated.

Map overlay: room graph with current room highlighted, visited rooms, doors. Draw styled blueprint.

UI: top-left health hearts, ability icons bottom? Minimap top-right? Could add small compass. Show objective hint ("Find a way deeper", etc.) at start of each room fade text.

Title screen: "SEWERFALL" maybe better name. Subtitle "A Metroidvania beneath New York". Show animated background with dripping, neon "NYC SEWER DEPT" sign. Buttons "Descend" / "Continue" if save exists. Instructions. Visually strong first impression.

Name: "BELOW THE BOROUGHS"? "SUMP CITY". "DOWNTOWN: Below". I like "SUMP CITY: A Metroidvania in the New York sewers". Title "SUMP CITY". Hmm maybe "SEWER RAT" ... Let's pick "SUMP CITY" with tagline "There's a whole city under the city."

Actually theme NYC sewers: Alligators-in-sewers myth -> Croc boss. Great. Title: "GATORTOWN"? "SEWERFALL". I'll go "SUMP CITY".

Implement files:
- index.html: canvas, title overlay, HUD DOM maybe canvas-drawn? DOM overlays easier for mobile controls and menus; game canvas renders world + HUD in canvas. Overlay screens DOM for title/pause/map/ending and touch controls. CSS responsive, safe areas.
- style.css
- game.js (main engine, could be ~2500 lines). Keep modules? Single JS is fine but large. Could split level.js, audio.js, game.js. Static server serves modules. Use ES modules? fine. But simpler single file avoids path issues. Yet editing giant file is harder. Split:
  - js/audio.js (synth)
  - js/levels.js (room definitions/builders)
  - js/game.js (engine/loop/render/UI wiring)
  - css/style.css
  - index.html

Testing with playwright. Need server in tmux. Let's set up tmux session per AGENTS. Check tmux installed and playwright config. Also maybe screenshot via playwright-cli requires session and Xvfb is preconfigured.

Let me inspect playwright-cli help and linux.json.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
---
{
  "outputDir": "/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/output",
  "browser": {
    "browserName": "chromium",
    "launchOptions": {
      "channel": "chromium",
      "headless": false,
      "args": ["--enable-gpu", "--ignore-gpu-blocklist", "--enable-unsafe-webgpu", "--use-angle=vulkan", "--enable-features=Vulkan", "--use-vulkan=swiftshader", "--use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader", "--disable-vulkan-surface"]
    }
  }
}

## Objective
- Build a playable Metroidvania game set in the sewers of New York, based on the user's one-line request: `"Metroidvania set in the sewers of new york"`.

## Requirements
- Static web game served from repo root via `index.html`.
- Metroidvania pillars: interconnected rooms, ability-gated progression, map, save/checkpoint, bosses.
- Mobile support: responsive layout and usable touch controls.
- User gave no further constraints.

## Decisions
- Original title **SUMP CITY**, tagline "There’s a whole city under the city."
- Pure Canvas 2D, no external assets; procedural vector/pixel art and WebAudio synthesis.
- Logical 960×540 resolution; HUD full-res, world rendered via adaptive lower-res offscreen canvas for software-renderer performance.
- 8 rooms: `hub`, `rats`, `tunnel7`, `steam`, `sump`, `overflow`, `secret`, `croclair`.
- Three relics: `grip` (wall jump, Tunnel 7), `boots` (double jump, Sump Warden), `dash` (Steamworks).
- Bosses: Sump Warden (mini-boss) and The Crocodile King (final boss).
- 6 tokens, 2 health cells, readable lore notes, two save benches (hub and overflow).
- Input: A/D, Space, J, Shift, W, M, Esc; touch D-pad + Jump/Hit/Dash/Interact.

## Work State
### Completed
- Wrote `index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/common.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/levels.js`, `js/render.js`, `js/game.js`.
- Implemented movement, jump, wall jump, double jump, dash, melee combat, breakables, enemies, hazards, pickups, notes, benches, save/load via localStorage, map overlay, pause, death/respawn, title, ending.
- Implemented all room layouts and bosses.
- Fixed module export error (`TOKEN_TOTAL`) and double-camera-offset rendering bug.
- Fixed static tile cache only covering top-left viewport (`drawTiles(def, cam, full)`).
- Removed hub spawn-overlapping platform at tile `(24,25,3,1)`.
- Added static room/background caching, sprite-based lighting at half res, CSS blend removal, adaptive render scale.
- Verified all room entry spawns except `hub/bottom` (now fixed in code but not re-verified).
- Captured screenshots in `screenshots/` (title, hub, rats, tunnel7, steam, etc.).

### Active
- Visual polish and lighting tuning: rooms are currently too dark/monochrome, enemies hard to see, graffiti oversized, title composition weak.
- Need to inspect `sump`, `overflow`, `secret`, `croclair` screenshots (captured, not yet reviewed).
- Need to verify gameplay traversal/transitions, bosses, map, mobile controls, and save/respawn.

### Blocked
- Screenshot automation in this environment runs under SwiftShader at ~16–20fps; performance is not representative of normal GPU browsers.
- Adaptive render scale currently drops to ~0.75; freeze during visual inspection with `SUMP.renderer.adaptScale=()=>{}; SUMP.renderer.setScale(1)`.
- Latest captured `tunnel7.png` and `steam.png` show the **WASHED OUT** death overlay because the player died before/during teleport inspection; re-capture after resetting HP/state.

## Next Move
1. Tune lighting: change `dark = 0.9 - def.light` to roughly `clamp(0.62 - def.light*0.7, 0.24, 0.55)`; increase lamp/player glow alpha.
2. Brighten tile palettes and enemy silhouettes (rats currently near-black), reduce graffiti font from 24px and alpha.

4. Re-verify `hub/bottom` spawn and all room entries programmatically; test right/left/up/down transitions in play.
5. Test and visually inspect `sump`, `overflow`, `secret`, `croclair`, bosses, pause/map/note/death/ending screens, and touch controls.
6. Verify save/continue/respawn and localStorage behavior; ensure objective hints and relic banners work.

## Objective
- Build a playable Metroidvania game set in the sewers of New York from the user’s request: `"Metroidvania set in the sewers of new york"`.

## Requirements
- Static browser game served from repo root via `index.html`.
- Metroidvania pillars: interconnected rooms, ability-gated progression, map, save/checkpoints, bosses.
- Mobile support: responsive layout and usable touch controls.
- User gave no further constraints.

## Decisions
- Original title **SUMP CITY**, tagline “There’s a whole city under the city.”
- Pure Canvas 2D; no external assets; procedural vector/pixel art and WebAudio synthesis.
- Logical 960×540 resolution; HUD full-res; world rendered through adaptive lower-res offscreen canvas.
- 8 rooms: `hub`, `rats`, `tunnel7`, `steam`, `sump`, `overflow`, `secret`, `croclair`.
- Relics: `grip` (wall jump, Tunnel 7), `boots` (double jump, Sump Warden), `dash` (Steamworks).
- Bosses: Sump Warden (mini-boss) and The Crocodile King (final boss).
- Collectibles now consistently total **6 tokens, 2 health cells, 3 relics**.
- Sump’s hidden reward changed from a seventh token to `cell-sump` to resolve the count mismatch and realize the intended second health cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented `index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/common.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/levels.js`, `js/render.js`, `js/game.js`.
- Implemented movement, jump, wall jump, double jump, dash, melee combat, breakables, enemies, hazards, pickups, notes, benches, save/load via localStorage, map overlay, pause, death/respawn, title, ending, and touch controls.
- Implemented all room layouts and bosses.
- Fixed input edge retention by clearing `edges` each frame.
- Fixed double jump: ground jump now sets `usedDouble = false`.
- Fixed hub progression: removed full-height right shaft wall, added bottom gap, and converted grating to a one-tile catwalk so the east side and Rats are reachable.
- Verified hub→rats transition works by holding right through the repaired shaft.
- Rebalanced lighting brighter: `clamp(0.62 - def.light * 0.6, 0.24, 0.52)`, stronger player/lamp clearance and glows.
- Brightened all room palettes, enemy silhouettes, and reduced graffiti size/alpha.
- Added lighting to the title scene.
- Removed duplicated dynamic-prop rendering and fixed foreground drip particles being drawn twice.
- Hid HUD during death/ending screens.
- Added `syncTouchUI()` and `body.in-game` so touch controls only appear during play.
- Moved mobile menu buttons below the token HUD.
- Added a full-screen portrait rotate overlay for coarse-pointer devices.
- Verified note screen, bench save/continue, death/respawn, warden defeat + boots pickup, croc defeat + ending, map, pause, and mobile touch movement.
- Captured updated screenshots in `screenshots/` with `polish-` prefix.

### Active
- Final regression pass after the latest patches: duplicate-prop removal, HUD hiding, mobile menu repositioning, portrait overlay, and retuned visuals.
- Need to verify wall-jump traversal up the hub shaft with `grip`, and the full ability-gated route through every room.
- Need to test actual boss combat, both health cells, breakables, barriers, and collectible completion in normal play.
- Need to validate all room entry spawns/collisions, including `hub/bottom`.
- Need to confirm mobile title screen hides touch controls and that touch menu placement is clear.

### Blocked
- Screenshot automation runs under SwiftShader at roughly 16–20 FPS; performance is not representative of normal GPU browsers.
- Portrait rotate overlay depends on `(pointer: coarse)`, so desktop emulation does not display it faithfully.
- Playwright’s `Space` key name did not trigger the game; use `" "` or JS-dispatched `KeyboardEvent({ code: 'Space' })`.

## Next Move
1. Reload after the latest patches and recapture title, hub, a mid-room, pause/map, mobile landscape, and mobile title screenshots.
2. Test wall-jumping up the hub central shaft with `grip` and verify the route into Overflow.
3. Play/test the full ability-gated route: Rats → Tunnel 7 → Steamworks → Sump → Overflow → Croc.
4. Test actual Warden/Croc combat, breakable walls, gates/barriers, both cells, and all six tokens.
5. Programmatically revalidate every room entry and confirm no spawn starts inside geometry, especially `hub/bottom`.
6. Confirm touch controls show only in play, hide on title/pause/map/death/ending, and remain usable in landscape.
7. Re-enable/observe adaptive scale and evaluate final FPS and screenshot quality.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: game state, physics, input, AI, bosses, progression, save/load, UI wiring, loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/render.js`: world/HUD/title/map rendering, lighting, static caches, adaptive resolution.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/levels.js`: 8 room layouts, props, enemies, items, entrances/exits, map layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/common.js`: constants, physics, themes, palettes, relic metadata, draw helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM screens, HUD overlays, touch controls.
